_instructions: Copy to content/collections/<slug>.json, delete this key, and read docs/EDITORIAL.md first. Order entries by the stage of the job, not by install count — the ordering is the expertise. Every skillSlug must exist in data/skills-index.json; never copy install counts or tiers into the notes, they're resolved live.
title: The N Skills Worth Installing for <theme>
description: One line under the H1. Say what the list is organised by, so it's clearly not a popularity ranking.

curator.name: TrustedSkills Editorial
curator.bio: Where the judgement comes from — the domain experience that makes this list worth more than a sort by downloads.

intro: Markdown. Set up the theme and who the list is for. The strongest opening is the one that explains why a naive list of the most-installed skills in this area is useless, then states the organising principle you used instead — usually the stages of the actual job, in order.
criteria:
Markdown. How the list was built: the inclusion tests each pick had to pass, and the tiebreak when two competed for a slot.

Then **what you deliberately left off, and why**. This is often the most useful section on the page and the hardest to fake — it's where real judgement shows.
evidenceNote: Markdown. Which entries have been run hands-on and which are shortlisted from registry signals (source, publisher, install base). Be plain about it. A curated list is allowed to be curated; it is not allowed to imply testing that didn't happen. Note that entries carrying a 🧪 Reviewed badge link to a hands-on review.

entries.role: Stage 1 — what job this pick does in the set
entries.note: Markdown. Why this skill earned this slot, and what to watch out for when you use it. Ground it in what's verifiable: the source, the publisher, the install base. If our own registry summary for it is weak or auto-generated, say so — that's a gap in our data, not a criticism of the author.
